samples.summary: Extra unbounded regex scan per replace amplifies the existing ReDoS surface in `Doc.searchText`
samples.evidence: `Doc.searchText` compiles the raw query with `new RegExp(query, flags)` when `useRegex` is on (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:908) with no pattern-complexity limit, no execution timeout and no worker — it runs on the UI thread over every block and every table cell. The diff adds a second full-document `this.search(...)` at the top of `replaceActive` (line 63) and `replaceAll` (line 86), so a single Replace / Replace All click now costs two whole-document regex sweeps instead of one (plus one per `replaceMatch` iteration path already present). Vector: a collaborator (or a docx import, see packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts) plants a long pathological run of text in a shared document; the local user's regex query then backtracks catastrophically and the tab hangs — the added pre-search doubles the time window and makes the hang reachable from the Replace button, not just from typing in the Find box. Self/peer-inflicted DoS on the client only; no server impact, which is why this is minor rather than major. Pre-existing weakness, amplified by this diff.
searchedFor: read packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx for any query length/complexity limit

samples.summary: replaceAll now rewrites matches the user was never shown (TOCTOU between displayed match count and written scope)
samples.evidence: The find bar gates the button on the *displayed* `matchCount` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:143,309) which is set from the last `syncHighlights()`. With the new `this.search(...)` at packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:86, the set actually written is recomputed at click time from the live CRDT document, which a remote peer can have grown in between (`store.onRemoteChange` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx). A malicious collaborator can therefore inject additional occurrences of the query after the local user reads '3 of 3' and have the local user's session rewrite them under the local user's identity/undo stack — the write scope exceeds what the UI presented for consent. Impact is bounded because the peer already holds edit rights on that document, so this is a confused-deputy/attribution concern rather than a privilege gain. `replaceActive` (line 63) has the same shape: the recomputed `matches[activeIndex]` need not be the highlighted match the user aimed at.
searchedFor: grep FindReplaceState|replaceActive|replaceAll across packages (only docs-find-bar.tsx calls them)

samples.summary: The pre-search added inside replaceActive/replaceAll is outside the find bar's invalid-regex try/catch
samples.evidence: `docs-find-bar.tsx:89-95` wraps `state.search(...)` in try/catch to degrade gracefully on a bad regex, but `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` (lines 136, 145) call `replaceActive`/`replaceAll` bare, and those now call `search()` internally (find-replace.ts:63, 86). Today `Doc.searchText` swallows `new RegExp` failures itself (document.ts:906-912) so no throw escapes, but the new call site relies on that implicit contract rather than the component's guard; any future search path that throws becomes an unhandled exception in a click handler. No security impact traced — noted for completeness.

samples.summary: No read-only bypass introduced: the viewer gate still holds on every path I could reach
samples.evidence: Checked as the primary hypothesis and could not break it. `replaceActive`/`replaceAll` are only constructed in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:65 from `editor.getDoc()`; under `readOnly` the editor builds its single `Doc` over `readOnlyDocStore(docStore)` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1142-1144), so `deleteText`/`insertText`/`batch`-inner writes and `snapshot()` are no-ops even if the new pre-search repopulates `matches` and skips the old early return. The component-level gate (`readOnly ||` at docs-find-bar.tsx:134,143 and the unrendered row at :288) is evaluated before the state call, and `readOnly` is forwarded from docs-view.tsx:686. After `dispose()` the `revocableDocStore` degrades to the same read-only handle. Reporting as an explicit negative so the verifier does not have to re-derive it.
